subject: Prepay wallet mechanics and escrow redemption for multi-year commit
messages:
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@aureliahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Exploring multi-year prepay w/ usage drawdown (Aurelia Health)

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Aurelia is excited about the latency profile and the telemetry. Procurement asked me to follow up on one thing our CFO flagged: we prefer a prepaid commitment but need the wallet to operate on a usage-first drawdown (monthly) with predictable ramping across years.

Key asks from our side:
- Example cadence for drawdown and true-up (monthly vs quarterly).
- How unused prepay gets handled at year boundaries (carry-forward vs escrow/refund).
- What discounts you can provide for a 3-year commitment with step-down pricing as usage ramps.
- Any SLA/credit language tied to committed throughput.

Can you send a short note on how Redwood structures this? If it helps, target commit is ~$1.2M in year 1 (ramp expected), $2.5M in year 2, $3.2M in year 3.

Jordan
Jordan Li
Director of AI Platforms, Aurelia Health

PS — copying procurement here for calendar/contract logistics.
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay w/ usage drawdown (Aurelia Health)

Jordan — appreciate the clarity. Summary below of a pragmatic structure that matches your asks; attaching a one-page mechanism and a short example wallet schedule (redwood_prepaid_mechanism_v1.pdf).

Proposed high-level model (usage-first drawdown, monthly true-up):
- Prepay wallet funded annually up front (invoiced per-year). Funds are consumed monthly on actual usage (token-based meter).
- Monthly true-up within 10 business days of month-end: if usage > wallet draw, we invoice overage at paygo rates or draw from a short-term reserve if agreed. If usage < funded amount, unused dollars go into an escrow bucket for the customer.
- Escrow redemption rules at year boundary: 1) Allow 12-month carry-forward for escrow balance to offset future months (preferred for growth customers). 2) After 12 months, remaining escrow can either be refunded (subject to admin fee) or converted to credits at a reduced discount rate (we typically convert at a 50% of original discount to avoid arbitrage).
- Ramp/discounting approach (example): Year 1 — 18% term discount off list, Year 2 — 10%, Year 3 — 6% (discount applied to token/unit rate). Discounts conditional on minimum annual draw thresholds.
- Optional escrow security: for multi-year deals we can hold Year 2/3 prepay in a restricted escrow ledger (not refunded) if customer wants deeper price protection.

Operational notes:
- Billing cadence: annual invoice for prepaid amount; monthly reporting and a detailed consumption CSV.
- SLA credits: available for committed throughput bands — apply as percentage credits against next invoice, subject to SLA measurement windows.
- Termination/early-exit: pro-rated refund on remaining unlocked wallet funds minus used credits and a 3% admin fee; locked escrow (if used for deeper discount) is non-refundable.

Next steps: 1) I can convert this into a short term sheet and pricing calc; 2) schedule a 30-min call to align on ramp thresholds and true-up cadence. Are you available Wed 12/16 10–11am PT?

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Aurelia Health — proposed discounts & escrow wording (need pricing sign-off)

Karthik/Ben —
Following Jordan's note (below) and our proposed mechanics, they gave target volumes. I sketched an initial discount ladder and escrow options; please see attached pricing calc (pricing_calc_sheet_v2.xlsx). Quick ask: confirm whether the following is feasible from a margin and risk perspective.

Proposal (draft):
- Commitment: 3-year term; Year 1 prepaid $1.2M, Year 2 prepaid $2.5M, Year 3 prepaid $3.2M.
- Discount ladder (applied to token/unit rates):
  * Year 1: 18% upfront (subject to min draw >= $1.0M)
  * Year 2: 12% upfront (subject to min draw >= $2.0M)
  * Year 3: 8% upfront (subject to min draw >= $3.0M)
- Escrow handling: Allow 12-month carry-forward. After 12 months, convert leftover escrow to credits at 50% of original discount unless customer chooses refund (refund admin fee 3%). If customer opts for locked escrow for Years 2/3, those funds are non-refundable and enable an additional 2% price pick-up.
- True-up cadence: monthly reporting + quarterly reconciliation (billing adjusts only at quarter boundaries).

Open questions for pricing: a) locked escrow risk exposure (we can require a larger up-front buffer), b) SLA credit sizing if they require committed throughput SLAs.

If we can accept the locked-escrow pick-up and the 50% conversion rule, I think this is a clean deal that preserves upside while capping refund risk.

Thoughts?
— Mina
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T11:54:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — proposed discounts & escrow wording (need pricing sign-off)

Mina —
I like the structure; a few pricing-risk tweaks I recommend:

1) Tweak discounts slightly to protect margin if usage under-indexes vs commit:
   - Y1: 16% (instead of 18%) with a make-good true-up if draw < 80% of committed volume by end of Y1.
   - Y2: 10% (instead of 12%); Y3: 6% (instead of 8%).
2) Locked escrow: require a 6-month minimum irrevocable lock for locked-escrow funds to reduce churn exposure. If they want the extra 2% pick-up, it should only apply if locked escrow >= 50% of that year's prepaid.
3) True-up cadence: keep monthly consumption reporting, but perform financial reconciliation quarterly; for smaller overages (<5% of annual commit) allow automatic draw from a short reserve to avoid surprise invoices.
4) SLA credits: cap credits to 5% of quarterly invoice and require documented incident postmortems to trigger recurring credits.

If you agree, I can update the calc and term sheet. Recommend including an explicit sample month-by-month amortization example in the appendix so procurement sees how carry-forward works.

— Karthik
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@aureliahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Finalized mechanics & next steps — RW-AH-1173 (term sheet incoming)

Jordan — thanks for the discussion earlier today. Per the call and internal feedback, summary of agreed mechanics and next steps: 

Agreed commercial mechanics:
- Prepay + monthly usage-first drawdown with monthly reporting, financial reconciliation quarterly.
- Discount ladder (finalized): Y1 16% | Y2 10% | Y3 6% (applies to token/unit list rate subject to committed thresholds).
- Escrow: 12-month carry-forward for unlocked escrow; option for locked escrow for Years 2/3 (6-month irrevocable lock) that yields an additional 2% price pick-up if locked-escrow >= 50% of that year's prepay.
- True-up & overage handling: overages drawn from short reserve (<=5% of annual commit) otherwise invoiced at paygo; quarterly reconciliation aligns final billing.
- SLA credits: capped at 5% of quarterly invoice, per Karthik's suggestion.
- Early termination: pro-rated refund on unlocked funds minus used credits and 3% admin fee; locked escrow non-refundable.

Attachments: I have attached the updated calc and a draft term sheet (RW-AH-1173-term-sheet-draft.pdf). I also pushed the deal to HubSpot (link below) and will open a DocuSign envelope once you confirm acceptance of the main mechanics.

Next steps for Aurelia: please confirm acceptance of the commercial mechanics above by reply and indicate whether you prefer: (A) refunds on post-12-month escrow leftovers or (B) automatic conversion to credits at 50% discount value. If you choose B we will bake conversion language into the term sheet.

From our side: once we have confirmation I'll issue the Year 1 invoice and route the term sheet for signatures (expected DocuSign link included).

Thanks — looking forward to partnering here.

— Mina
